budget_items.what_was_said: The chair reviewed a 2017 dispersement from the worthy poor fund's earnings to a resident, structured as a loan with a six-month redetermination that was never followed up on. He said this board will now have to take up that redetermination.
Reading a 1966 record at the Worcester Savings Institute, the chair cited the fund's total, its original principal, and interest recorded as of a 1965 date.

budget_items.topic: Nathaniel Day fund and missing Treasury bond
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair read the Nathaniel Day fund's savings balance and noted a 90-day Treasury bond in that fund that he cannot locate; he wants to find where it is and whether it was cashed.

The chair said Susan Howard's separate fund (distinct from the sidewalk fund) held Treasury bonds, and estimated informally what decades of compounding might now be worth if the bonds were never cashed.

budget_items.topic: Sidewalk (John and Mary Caldwell Howard) fund, 1931
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair read the 1931 warrant article establishing the fund with a stated principal and annual interest amount, to be spent on sidewalks and public grounds within one mile of town center in perpetuity.

A commissioner asked why the fund shows a much lower current balance than what decades of interest at the stated rate should have produced; the chair said he has to find where the money went and will pursue it.
The chair read two 1931 warrant articles accepting sums for perpetual care of specific cemetery lots in the North Cemetery.

A 2013 letter setting up the fund specified that only annual interest could be dispersed, capped at a share of that year's interest, until the fund passed a threshold at which principal above that amount could also be used for veterans' benefits.

decisions.decision: Chair and vice chair will brainstorm a bylaw allowing the select board to release trust fund money in the absence of a quorum, to be drafted by the chair as a hard copy for the next meeting.
The commission wants a public comment period built into the process before finalizing bylaw changes and any cy pres filing, even though it is not legally required.
The chair will personally contact individuals named in the 2017 meeting minutes to recover missing trust fund records rather than wait for them to come forward.
The chair will investigate the unexplained 'Lind Saxon' fund from 2017 with the accounting department, since no records or dispersements for it can be found.
A cy pres court filing to update the American Legion veterans fund's restrictions will wait until after the next election cycle due to the town attorney's town meeting workload.
The chair will contact the U.S. Treasury to try to locate the Nathaniel Day fund's Treasury bond and determine its status.
The chair will investigate why the sidewalk (Howard) fund's current balance is far below what decades of stated interest should have produced.
Interns will not be used this year due to lack of a prepared curriculum; it may be revisited next year.
The commission has an open vacancy and is inviting interested residents to come forward.

minutes.summary: The Trust Fund Commission (chair John Bowen and vice chair Richard Howard, the only two present) spent most of the meeting reviewing decades of historic trust fund records ahead of drafting a bylaw that would let the select board release trust fund money when the commission lacks a quorum. In the process the chair identified an unresolved 2017 loan redetermination, a fund from 2017 with no discoverable records, and a large apparent gap between what a 1931 sidewalk/memorial fund should be worth today and its current balance, all of which he committed to investigate further. No formal votes were taken except the roll-call vote to adjourn.

what_happened.line: The chair found the 1931 sidewalk memorial fund's current balance far below what decades of stated interest should have produced and will investigate where the money went.
The commission began drafting a bylaw letting the select board release trust fund money when the commission itself lacks a quorum.
An unresolved 2017 loan redetermination tied to a worthy-poor-fund dispersement surfaced and this board will now have to take it up.
The chair flagged a 2017 fund with no discoverable records and will pursue it with the accounting department.
The commission agreed to build a public comment period into the bylaw and any related court filing, even though not legally required.

why_it_matters: These are the town's historic trust and memorial funds, meant to pay for things like sidewalks, veterans' benefits and cemetery care, so unresolved records affect whether that money can still be used as intended.
The proposed bylaw would change who can authorize releasing trust fund money when this commission cannot meet, a procedural change residents may see come to a vote.
The commission has an open seat and is inviting residents to apply.
